name: Acetaminophen
uses: Pain and fever.
side: Liver effects at high doses. Toxic to cats.
how: Reduces pain and fever through effects in the brain.
avoid: People with liver disease or heavy alcohol use. Toxic to cats and dangerous for dogs.

name: Acetazolamide
uses: Glaucoma, altitude sickness and some fluid conditions.
how: Blocks carbonic anhydrase, reducing fluid production in the eye and elsewhere.
avoid: People with a sulfa allergy, kidney or liver disease, or low sodium or potassium.

name: Adapalene
uses: Acne.
how: A retinoid that normalizes skin cell turnover and calms inflammation.
avoid: Pregnancy. Increases sun sensitivity.

name: Alendronate
uses: Bone loss and, in cats, some types of high calcium.
side: Esophageal irritation; take with water as directed.
how: Slows the cells that break down bone.
avoid: People or pets with swallowing problems or esophageal disease; give with plenty of water.

name: Alpha lipoic acid
uses: Antioxidant supplement for nerve support. Toxic to cats.
how: An antioxidant involved in energy metabolism.
avoid: Cats (it is toxic to them). People with diabetes should monitor blood sugar.

name: Aluminum hydroxide
uses: Phosphate binder for pets with kidney disease.
how: Binds phosphorus in food so less is absorbed.
avoid: Long-term use needs monitoring; give with meals.

name: Amantadine
uses: Chronic pain in dogs and cats; Parkinson's in people.
how: Blocks NMDA receptors involved in chronic pain and increases dopamine.
avoid: People or pets with kidney disease or seizures.

name: Amikacin
uses: Resistant bacterial infections, including vet ear preparations.
how: An aminoglycoside that stops bacteria from making proteins.
avoid: Ruptured eardrums (ear products) and kidney disease.

name: Amitriptyline
uses: Nerve pain, sleep and mood in people; anxiety, itch and bladder pain in pets; also in topical pain creams.
how: A tricyclic that increases serotonin and norepinephrine and calms nerve pain signals.
avoid: People or pets with heart rhythm problems, glaucoma or urinary retention, and anyone on MAO inhibitors.

name: Amlodipine
uses: High blood pressure in people and especially cats.
side: Ankle swelling, flushing, low blood pressure, gum overgrowth in dogs.
how: Relaxes blood vessels by blocking calcium from entering the muscle in their walls.
avoid: People or pets with very low blood pressure or severe heart valve narrowing.

name: Ammonium chloride
uses: Acidifies urine to help dissolve or prevent certain bladder stones in pets.
how: Makes the urine more acidic.
avoid: Pets with liver or kidney disease.

name: Amoxicillin
uses: Bacterial infections.
how: A penicillin antibiotic that breaks down bacterial cell walls.
avoid: Anyone with a penicillin allergy. Not for rabbits, guinea pigs and some other small mammals.

name: Amoxicillin/clavulanate
uses: Bacterial infections.
how: Amoxicillin plus clavulanate, which protects it from bacterial enzymes that would destroy it.
avoid: Anyone with a penicillin allergy. Not for rabbits and guinea pigs.

name: Amphotericin B
uses: Nasal and sinus rinses for fungal sinus conditions.
how: Binds fungal cell membranes and makes them leak.
avoid: Usually well tolerated as a nasal rinse; not for use without a prescriber's direction.

name: Anastrozole
uses: An aromatase inhibitor that lowers estrogen; used in breast cancer care and sometimes alongside testosterone therapy.
how: Blocks aromatase, the enzyme that converts testosterone into estrogen, lowering estrogen levels.
avoid: Premenopausal women (unless prescribed alongside other therapy), people with osteoporosis, and those who are pregnant.

name: Apomorphine
uses: Induces vomiting in dogs after a toxic ingestion, given by a veterinarian.
how: Stimulates dopamine receptors in the brain's vomiting center.
avoid: Cats (usually), and pets that are unconscious, having seizures or swallowed something caustic or sharp.

name: Aripiprazole
uses: Mood disorders and, in low doses, other conditions as prescribed.
how: Partially activates dopamine and serotonin receptors, stabilizing their signals.
avoid: Older adults with dementia and people with a history of seizures.

name: Atenolol
uses: High blood pressure and heart rhythm or heart muscle conditions in people and cats.
side: Tiredness, slow heart rate, low blood pressure.
how: A beta-blocker that slows the heart and lowers blood pressure.
avoid: People or pets with asthma, very slow heart rate or uncontrolled heart failure. Do not stop suddenly.

name: Azathioprine
uses: Immune-mediated diseases in dogs.
side: Vomiting, bone marrow and liver effects; requires monitoring. Not for cats.
how: Interferes with the growth of immune cells.
avoid: Cats (it can cause serious bone marrow suppression), pregnancy, and people or dogs with low TPMT enzyme activity.

name: Azelaic acid
uses: Acne, rosacea and dark spots.
how: Reduces acne bacteria, calms redness and slows pigment production.
avoid: People with a history of cold sores near the application area.
Sun exposure, which makes melasma worse. Use sunscreen daily.
how: Azelaic acid, kojic acid and vitamin C each slow pigment production, and niacinamide reduces the transfer of pigment to the skin surface.
name: Azelaic acid and kojic acid melasma cream
side: Stinging, itching, redness or dryness, usually mild and early in treatment.
uses: Melasma and dark spots, without hydroquinone. Made with azelaic acid 18%, kojic acid 4%, niacinamide 3% and vitamin C 2%.

avoid: Sun exposure, which makes melasma worse. Use sunscreen daily.
how: Tranexamic acid calms the signals that switch on pigment cells. Azelaic acid and kojic acid slow pigment production, and niacinamide reduces the transfer of pigment to the skin surface.
name: Azelaic acid and tranexamic acid melasma cream
side: Stinging, itching, redness or dryness, usually mild and early in treatment.
uses: Melasma and dark spots, without hydroquinone. Made with azelaic acid 12%, tranexamic acid 5%, kojic acid 4% and niacinamide 3%.

name: Azithromycin
uses: Bacterial and some respiratory and parasitic infections.
how: A macrolide antibiotic that stops bacteria from making proteins.
avoid: People or pets with liver disease or heart rhythm problems.

name: Baclofen
uses: Muscle spasm, including in topical pain and vaginal creams.
how: Activates GABA-B receptors to relax muscle spasm.
avoid: People with kidney disease or seizures. Toxic to dogs in overdose; keep away from pets.

name: BEG nasal spray
uses: A compounded nasal spray combining mupirocin (Bactroban), EDTA and gentamicin, prescribed for chronic sinus infections, often after sinus surgery.
side: Nasal stinging, burning or irritation, and occasional nosebleeds.
how: EDTA helps break up bacterial biofilms, the protective layers bacteria form in the sinuses, so the antibiotics mupirocin and gentamicin can reach the bacteria.
avoid: People allergic to mupirocin or aminoglycoside antibiotics such as gentamicin. Use only as long as directed and follow up with your prescriber.

name: Benazepril
uses: High blood pressure, heart failure and kidney protein loss, especially in cats and dogs.
side: Low blood pressure, decreased appetite, changes in kidney values.
how: An ACE inhibitor that relaxes blood vessels and reduces protein loss through the kidneys.
avoid: Pregnancy, and people or pets with dehydration or high potassium.

name: Benzocaine
uses: Numbing agent in topical anesthetic creams.
side: Local irritation; rare blood oxygen problem (methemoglobinemia).
how: Blocks nerve signals to numb the skin or mouth.
avoid: Children under 2 and people with methemoglobinemia.

name: Betahistine
uses: Vertigo and Meniere's disease.
how: Acts on histamine receptors and may improve blood flow in the inner ear.
avoid: People with active stomach ulcers, asthma or pheochromocytoma.

name: Betamethasone
uses: Potent steroid for inflamed skin and nipple cream formulas.
how: A potent steroid that reduces inflammation.
avoid: Untreated skin infections; avoid long use on the face or thin skin.

name: Bethanechol
uses: Helps the bladder empty in people and pets.
how: Stimulates the bladder muscle to contract.
avoid: People or pets with urinary or bowel blockages, asthma or slow heart rate.

name: Biest (estriol + estradiol)
uses: A combination of estriol and estradiol, usually 80/20 or 50/50, for menopausal hormone therapy.
how: Combines two estrogens, estriol and estradiol, to replace estrogen after menopause.
avoid: People with a history of breast or uterine cancer, blood clots, stroke, liver disease or unexplained vaginal bleeding.

name: Biotin
uses: Hair, skin and nail support supplement.
side: Can interfere with some lab tests.
how: A B vitamin used by enzymes that support hair, skin and nails.
avoid: Tell your lab before blood tests, since biotin can skew some results.

name: BLT numbing cream
uses: A strong topical anesthetic combining benzocaine, lidocaine and tetracaine, applied before cosmetic and skin procedures such as injections, laser treatments and tattooing.
side: Redness, swelling or paleness of the skin. Using too much, on large areas or under a wrap can cause serious reactions affecting the heart or blood oxygen.
how: All three ingredients block sodium channels in nerve endings, stopping pain signals from traveling.
avoid: Applying to large areas, broken skin or under a wrap unless directed; people with methemoglobinemia or an allergy to local anesthetics. Keep away from children and pets.

name: Boric acid
uses: Vaginal suppositories for recurrent yeast and bacterial vaginosis.
how: Makes the vaginal environment hostile to yeast and some bacteria.
avoid: Pregnancy, and never take by mouth.

name: Brimonidine
uses: Facial redness from rosacea.
how: Narrows blood vessels in the skin to reduce redness.
avoid: Use as directed; overuse can cause rebound redness.

name: Budesonide
uses: Inflammatory bowel disease and other inflammation, with fewer whole-body steroid effects.
side: Increased thirst and appetite, mild steroid effects.
how: A steroid that acts mainly in the gut and is largely broken down by the liver before reaching the rest of the body.
avoid: People or pets with liver disease or active infections.

name: Bupropion
uses: Depression and smoking cessation.
side: Dry mouth, trouble sleeping, headache, anxiety.
how: Increases dopamine and norepinephrine in the brain.
avoid: People with seizure disorders or eating disorders, and anyone stopping alcohol or sedatives abruptly.

name: Buspirone
uses: Anxiety in people; anxiety and urine marking in cats.
how: Acts on serotonin receptors to reduce anxiety without heavy sedation.
avoid: Anyone taking MAO inhibitors, and people with severe liver or kidney disease.

name: Cabergoline
uses: High prolactin in people; false pregnancy and some reproductive uses in dogs.
how: Stimulates dopamine receptors to lower prolactin.
avoid: Pregnant pets (unless intended), and people with heart valve disease or uncontrolled blood pressure.

name: Caffeine
uses: Ingredient in topical hair-growth serums.
how: Stimulates hair follicles when applied to the scalp.
avoid: Usually well tolerated topically. Toxic to pets if swallowed.

name: Calcipotriene
uses: Psoriasis and some skin growths.
how: A vitamin D analog that slows skin cell overgrowth.
avoid: People with high calcium. Toxic to pets.

name: Calcitriol
uses: Active vitamin D for calcium balance in kidney disease and low parathyroid function.
how: The active form of vitamin D, which helps the body absorb calcium and controls parathyroid hormone.
avoid: People or pets with high calcium or high phosphorus.

name: Calcium carbonate
uses: Calcium supplement and phosphate binder.
how: A mineral supplement that also binds phosphorus in food.
avoid: People or pets with high calcium or kidney stones.

name: Calcium pantothenate
uses: Vitamin B5 supplement, often in hair formulas.
how: Vitamin B5, used in energy metabolism and skin health.
avoid: Usually well tolerated.

name: Capsaicin
uses: Topical pain relief.
how: Depletes substance P from nerve endings, reducing pain signals over time.
avoid: Broken skin, eyes and mucous membranes; wash hands after use.

name: Carprofen
uses: Arthritis and pain after surgery in dogs.
side: Stomach upset, liver and kidney effects.
how: A veterinary NSAID that reduces inflammation and pain.
avoid: Cats, and dogs with liver or kidney disease or taking steroids.

name: Cefpodoxime
uses: Skin and urinary infections in dogs.
how: A cephalosporin antibiotic that breaks down bacterial cell walls.
avoid: Pets with a cephalosporin allergy.

name: Ceftazidime
uses: Bacterial infections, including specialty topical preparations.
how: A cephalosporin antibiotic active against Pseudomonas.
avoid: People or pets with a cephalosporin allergy.

name: Cephalexin
uses: Skin and other bacterial infections.
how: A cephalosporin antibiotic that breaks down bacterial cell walls.
avoid: People with a serious penicillin or cephalosporin allergy.

name: Cetirizine
uses: Allergy and itch relief.
how: An antihistamine that blocks H1 receptors.
avoid: People or pets with kidney or liver disease (lower dose).

name: Chlorambucil
uses: Some cancers and immune diseases in cats and dogs, especially small-cell lymphoma in cats.
side: Bone marrow suppression; hazardous drug requiring careful handling.
how: Damages DNA in rapidly dividing cells, such as cancer and immune cells.
avoid: Pregnancy. Hazardous drug: wear gloves and never split or crush.

name: Chloramphenicol
uses: Resistant bacterial infections.
side: Bone marrow effects; hazardous for people handling it.
how: Stops bacteria from making proteins.
avoid: Pregnancy and people handling it with bare hands; can cause serious blood disorders in people.

name: Chlorpheniramine
uses: Allergy and itch relief; commonly used for cats.
how: A sedating antihistamine that blocks H1 receptors.
avoid: People or pets with glaucoma, urinary retention or heart disease.

name: Cholecalciferol (vitamin D3)
uses: Vitamin D supplement.
how: Vitamin D3, which the body converts to active vitamin D for calcium balance.
avoid: Too much can cause high calcium; accidental ingestion is dangerous for dogs.

name: Cholestyramine
uses: Bile acid binder; in barrier ointments for diaper and perianal skin irritation.
how: Binds bile acids, which can irritate skin in diaper and perianal areas.
avoid: Open wounds.

name: Cinacalcet
uses: High parathyroid hormone and high calcium.
how: Makes the parathyroid gland more sensitive to calcium, lowering parathyroid hormone.
avoid: People or pets with low calcium or seizures.

name: Ciprofloxacin
uses: Bacterial infections.
side: Stomach upset, tendon problems in people.
how: A fluoroquinolone that blocks bacterial DNA copying.
avoid: Children, people over 60 on steroids (tendon risk), and people with myasthenia gravis.

name: Cisapride
uses: Constipation and megacolon in cats and slow stomach emptying in pets; available only by compounding.
how: Stimulates serotonin (5-HT4) receptors in the gut to strengthen movement of the stomach and colon.
avoid: Pets with a bowel blockage or heart rhythm problems, or taking antifungals like ketoconazole. No longer sold commercially, so it is available only by compounding.

name: Clindamycin
uses: Skin, dental and bone infections; acne creams; toxoplasmosis in cats.
how: Stops bacteria from making proteins; especially active against anaerobes and toxoplasma.
avoid: Rabbits, guinea pigs and hamsters. People with a history of C. diff colitis.

name: Clobetasol
uses: Very potent steroid for stubborn skin conditions such as lichen sclerosus and psoriasis.
side: Skin thinning; use only as directed.
how: A very potent steroid for short-term use on stubborn inflammation.
avoid: Use on the face, groin or large areas only when directed; not for long-term use.

name: Clomiphene
uses: Ovulation induction in women and, off-label, support of natural testosterone production in men.
side: Hot flashes, mood changes, visual disturbances, headache.
how: Blocks estrogen's signal in the brain, which prompts the pituitary gland to release more of the hormones that drive ovulation and testosterone production.
avoid: People with liver disease, ovarian cysts, unexplained uterine bleeding or vision problems, and those who are pregnant.

name: Clomipramine
uses: Obsessive-compulsive disorder in people; separation anxiety and compulsive behaviors in dogs and cats.
how: A tricyclic that increases serotonin and norepinephrine.
avoid: People or pets with heart rhythm problems, glaucoma or seizures, and anyone on MAO inhibitors.

name: Clonidine
uses: Blood pressure, ADHD and sleep in people; anxiety in dogs.
side: Drowsiness, dry mouth, low blood pressure.
how: Stimulates alpha-2 receptors in the brain to reduce stress signals and lower blood pressure.
avoid: People or pets with slow heart rate or low blood pressure. Do not stop suddenly.

name: Clopidogrel
uses: Prevents blood clots in people and in cats with heart disease.
how: Keeps platelets from sticking together, reducing the risk of clots.
avoid: People or pets with active bleeding, bleeding disorders or upcoming surgery.

name: Coenzyme Q10
uses: Heart and energy support supplement.
how: A compound cells use to make energy, with antioxidant effects.
avoid: People taking warfarin.

name: Collagen
uses: Skin, hair and joint support supplement.
how: Protein building blocks for skin, hair and joints.
avoid: People with allergies to the source (fish, beef or other).

name: Combination hormone preparations
uses: Two or more hormones, such as estriol, estradiol, estrone, progesterone, testosterone, DHEA and pregnenolone, combined in one cream, troche, capsule or vaginal preparation, in the amounts and ratio your prescriber orders.
side: Depends on the hormones included. May include breast tenderness, spotting, bloating, acne, hair growth or irritation where applied.
how: Each hormone works as it does on its own. Combining them lets you use a single preparation for your prescribed doses instead of several separate ones.
avoid: People with a history of hormone-sensitive cancer, blood clots, stroke, liver disease or unexplained vaginal bleeding. Your prescriber monitors your hormone levels and symptoms.

name: Cyanocobalamin (vitamin B12)
uses: Vitamin B12 supplement, including flavored liquids for pets.
how: Vitamin B12, needed for nerve function and red blood cells.
avoid: Usually well tolerated.

name: Cyclosporine
uses: Immune-mediated disease and allergic skin disease in pets; dry eye.
how: Blocks activation of T cells, a key part of the immune response.
avoid: People or pets with cancer, serious infections, or kidney or liver disease.

name: Cyproheptadine
uses: Allergies in people; appetite stimulation in cats.
side: Drowsiness, dry mouth, excitability in cats.
how: Blocks histamine and serotonin receptors, which reduces allergy symptoms and stimulates appetite.
avoid: People or pets with glaucoma or urinary retention.

name: D-Penicillamine
uses: Copper storage disease and some stone types.
how: Binds copper and some other metals so the body can remove them.
avoid: People or pets with kidney disease or a penicillin allergy.

name: Dexamethasone
uses: Inflammation and allergic conditions; used in mouthwashes and ear preparations.
side: Increased thirst and appetite, mood changes.
how: A long-acting, potent steroid that calms inflammation.
avoid: People or pets with diabetes, infections or ulcers.

name: DHEA
uses: A hormone precursor sometimes prescribed for low DHEA levels and in vaginal preparations for menopause-related dryness.
side: Acne, oily skin, hair growth, mood changes.
how: DHEA is a hormone made by the adrenal glands that the body converts into testosterone and estrogen.
avoid: People with hormone-sensitive cancers, polycystic ovary syndrome or liver disease, and those who are pregnant.

name: Diazoxide
uses: Low blood sugar from insulin-secreting tumors in dogs.
how: Blocks insulin release from the pancreas, raising blood sugar.
avoid: Pets with heart failure or low blood pressure.

name: Diclofenac
uses: Anti-inflammatory for joint and muscle pain, including topical creams.
side: Skin irritation; stomach and kidney effects with oral use.
how: An NSAID that blocks COX enzymes to reduce inflammation and pain.
avoid: People with stomach ulcers, kidney disease or heart disease, and late pregnancy. Toxic to pets.

name: Diethylstilbestrol (DES)
uses: Estrogen-responsive urinary incontinence in spayed female dogs.
side: Bone marrow effects at high doses; requires monitoring.
how: A synthetic estrogen that strengthens the urethral sphincter in spayed female dogs.
avoid: Intact female dogs and cats. Doses are kept low and infrequent because high doses can suppress bone marrow.

name: Diltiazem
uses: Heart rhythm and blood pressure; topical forms for anal fissures.
side: Low blood pressure, slow heart rate, headache.
how: Blocks calcium channels in the heart and blood vessels, slowing heart rate and relaxing muscle.
avoid: People or pets with very low blood pressure or certain heart block conditions.

name: Diphenhydramine
uses: Allergies and itch; a common ingredient in mouthwash blends.
how: A sedating antihistamine that blocks H1 receptors.
avoid: People or pets with glaucoma, urinary retention or heart disease, and older adults.

name: Diphenoxylate/atropine
uses: Diarrhea.
how: Slows movement of the intestines; atropine is added to discourage misuse.
avoid: Children, and people or pets with infectious diarrhea or liver disease.

name: DMSA (succimer)
uses: A chelating agent that binds heavy metals such as lead so the body can remove them.
side: Nausea, diarrhea, rash, changes in liver values; requires monitoring.
how: Binds heavy metals such as lead so they can be removed through the urine.
avoid: People or pets with kidney or liver disease. Needs lab monitoring.

name: DMSO
uses: Carrier that helps medications absorb through the skin.
side: Garlic-like breath or taste, skin irritation.
how: A solvent that carries other medicines through the skin.
avoid: Apply only to clean skin, since it can carry other substances in with it.

name: Doxycycline
uses: Bacterial and tick-borne infections, acne and rosacea.
side: Stomach upset, sun sensitivity; give with water or food.
how: A tetracycline antibiotic that stops bacteria from making proteins; also calms inflammation in acne and rosacea.
avoid: Children under 8 and pregnancy. Give with water and food to protect the esophagus, especially in cats.

name: Drospirenone
uses: A progestin used in hormone therapy and contraception.
side: Headache, breast tenderness, nausea; can raise potassium.
how: A progestin that acts like progesterone and also has mild anti-androgen and water-balancing effects.
avoid: People with kidney or adrenal problems, liver disease, or a history of blood clots, and those taking medicines that raise potassium.

name: Duloxetine
uses: Depression, anxiety and nerve or chronic pain.
how: Increases both serotonin and norepinephrine, which affect mood and pain signals.
avoid: People with liver disease, heavy alcohol use or uncontrolled glaucoma, and those on MAO inhibitors.

name: Dutasteride
uses: Hair loss and enlarged prostate.
how: Blocks both forms of the enzyme that converts testosterone into DHT.
avoid: Anyone who is or may become pregnant should avoid handling it. People with liver disease.

name: Ear packs (veterinary)
uses: Long-acting ear preparations that combine an antibiotic, antifungal and steroid, applied by the veterinarian or at home as directed.
how: Combines medicines that kill bacteria and yeast with a steroid that calms inflammation, held in the ear canal for days.
avoid: Pets with a ruptured eardrum, unless the veterinarian has confirmed it is safe.

name: EDTA (tris-EDTA)
uses: Helps topical, nasal and ear antibiotics work better against biofilms.
how: Binds calcium and magnesium in bacterial cell walls and biofilms, making bacteria easier to kill.
avoid: Ruptured eardrums (ear products).

name: Enalapril
uses: High blood pressure, heart failure and protein loss through the kidneys.
side: Low blood pressure, cough in people, changes in kidney values.
how: An ACE inhibitor that relaxes blood vessels and reduces protein loss through the kidneys.
avoid: Pregnancy, and people or pets with severe kidney disease, dehydration or high potassium.

name: Enclomiphene
uses: A form of clomiphene prescribed off-label to help men's bodies make more of their own testosterone while preserving fertility.
side: Headache, hot flashes, mood changes, visual disturbances.
how: Blocks estrogen's signal in the brain, prompting the pituitary to release hormones that stimulate natural testosterone production.
avoid: People with liver disease, vision problems or high red blood cell counts.

name: Enrofloxacin
uses: Bacterial infections in pets, including ear packs.
side: Stomach upset; not for young, growing animals.
how: A fluoroquinolone that blocks bacterial DNA copying.
avoid: Young growing dogs (cartilage damage) and cats at high doses (vision damage).

name: Ergocalciferol (vitamin D2)
uses: Vitamin D supplement.
how: Vitamin D2, which the body converts to active vitamin D.
avoid: Too much can cause high calcium.

name: Ergoloid mesylates
uses: Circulation-supporting ingredient used in topical sexual-health creams.
how: Ergot-derived compounds that increase blood flow in small vessels.
avoid: People with low blood pressure or slow heart rate, and those taking other ergot medicines.

name: Erythromycin
uses: Bacterial infections and slow stomach emptying.
how: A macrolide antibiotic; at low doses it also stimulates the stomach to empty.
avoid: People or pets taking cisapride or other drugs it interacts with.

name: Estradiol
uses: Estrogen replacement for menopause symptoms such as hot flashes and vaginal dryness.
side: Breast tenderness, bloating, nausea, headache, spotting. Estrogen therapy carries boxed-warning risks your prescriber will review.
how: Replaces estradiol, the main estrogen the ovaries make before menopause.
avoid: People with a history of breast or uterine cancer, blood clots, stroke, heart attack, liver disease or unexplained vaginal bleeding, and those who are pregnant.

name: Estriol
uses: A milder estrogen used mainly in vaginal and topical preparations for menopause-related dryness and skin changes.
side: Vaginal irritation or discharge, breast tenderness, spotting.
how: A weaker estrogen that acts mainly on vaginal and skin tissue at the doses usually prescribed.
avoid: People with a history of estrogen-sensitive cancer, blood clots or unexplained vaginal bleeding.
Pregnancy. People who have been told to avoid estrogen, such as those with an estrogen-sensitive cancer, unless their prescriber approves. Use sunscreen daily.
how: Estriol, a mild estrogen, supports skin thickness, collagen and moisture. Tretinoin speeds skin cell turnover, and hyaluronic acid holds moisture.
name: Estriol and tretinoin anti-aging cream
side: Dryness, peeling or sun sensitivity. Estriol is a hormone, and a small amount can be absorbed through the skin.
uses: Aging skin and fine lines on the face and neck. Made with estriol 0.3%, hyaluronic acid 0.5% and tretinoin 0.02%.

name: Famciclovir
uses: Herpes infections in people and feline herpesvirus in cats.
how: Converted to penciclovir, which stops herpesviruses from copying their DNA.
avoid: People or pets with kidney disease (lower dose).

name: Famotidine
uses: Reduces stomach acid for reflux and ulcers.
how: Blocks histamine (H2) receptors in the stomach to reduce acid.
avoid: People or pets with kidney disease (lower dose).

name: Finasteride
uses: Hair loss (androgenetic alopecia) and enlarged prostate, including topical formulas for hair.
side: Decreased libido, sexual side effects, breast tenderness.
how: Blocks the enzyme that converts testosterone into DHT, the hormone behind male-pattern hair loss and prostate growth.
avoid: Anyone who is or may become pregnant should not handle crushed tablets or topical forms, since it can affect a developing baby.

name: Fluconazole
uses: Fungal and yeast infections.
how: Blocks the fungal enzyme needed to build the fungal cell membrane.
avoid: People with liver disease or heart rhythm problems, and pregnancy.

name: Fluorouracil
uses: Precancerous skin spots and warts, as prescribed.
how: Blocks DNA production in rapidly dividing abnormal skin cells.
avoid: Pregnancy. Extremely toxic to dogs and cats, even in small amounts; store securely.

name: Fluoxetine
uses: Depression and anxiety in people; anxiety, aggression and compulsive behaviors in dogs and cats.
side: Nausea, decreased appetite, sleep changes, restlessness.
how: An SSRI that increases serotonin available in the brain.
avoid: Anyone taking MAO inhibitors, tramadol or other serotonin medicines; pets with seizures. Takes several weeks to reach full effect.

name: Furosemide
uses: Fluid buildup from heart failure and other conditions.
how: A loop diuretic that makes the kidneys remove more salt and water.
avoid: People or pets who are dehydrated or have low potassium; needs kidney monitoring.

name: Gabapentin
uses: Nerve pain and seizures in people; pain, anxiety before vet visits and seizures in dogs and cats; also used in topical pain creams.
how: Binds calcium channels on nerve cells and reduces the release of pain and excitement signals.
avoid: People with kidney disease (dose adjustment needed). Liquids made for people may contain xylitol, which is toxic to dogs; pet formulations are made without it.

name: Gemfibrozil
uses: High triglycerides, including in dogs with high blood fats.
how: Lowers triglycerides by activating PPAR-alpha in the liver.
avoid: People or pets with liver, kidney or gallbladder disease, or taking statins.

name: Gentamicin
uses: Topical and ear and nasal preparations for bacterial infections.
how: An aminoglycoside that stops bacteria from making proteins.
avoid: Ruptured eardrums (ear products), and kidney disease if absorbed.

name: Glycolic acid
uses: Exfoliation for skin tone and texture.
how: An alpha hydroxy acid that loosens dead skin cells.
avoid: Sensitive or broken skin. Increases sun sensitivity.

name: Gonadorelin
uses: A synthetic form of the hormone that signals the pituitary gland, prescribed off-label to support natural testosterone and fertility signaling, often alongside testosterone therapy.
side: Headache, flushing, nausea, mouth irritation with troches.
how: Mimics GnRH, the brain hormone that signals the pituitary to release LH and FSH.
avoid: People with hormone-sensitive cancers or pituitary conditions.

name: Griseofulvin
uses: Ringworm and fungal infections.
how: Stops fungal cells from dividing.
avoid: Pregnancy, cats with FIV, and people with liver disease or porphyria.

name: GS-441524
uses: Antiviral used to treat feline infectious peritonitis (FIP) in cats, by veterinary prescription.
side: Mild stomach upset and changes in liver values; dosing is weight-based and set by your veterinarian.
how: A nucleoside analog that stops the feline coronavirus that causes FIP from copying its genetic material.
avoid: Treatment must be directed by a veterinarian with weight-based dosing and regular checkups, usually for at least 12 weeks.

name: Guaifenesin
uses: Loosens chest congestion.
how: Thins mucus so it is easier to clear.
avoid: Usually well tolerated; check combination products for other ingredients.

name: Guanfacine
uses: ADHD and blood pressure.
side: Drowsiness, low blood pressure, dry mouth.
how: Stimulates alpha-2 receptors in the brain, lowering blood pressure and improving focus.
avoid: People with slow heart rate or low blood pressure. Do not stop suddenly.

name: Hyaluronic acid
uses: Moisture for skin and vaginal tissue in creams.
how: A natural sugar molecule that holds water in skin and tissue.
avoid: Usually well tolerated.

name: Hydrochlorothiazide
uses: Blood pressure, fluid buildup and prevention of some urinary stones.
how: A thiazide diuretic that increases salt and water removal and reduces calcium in the urine.
avoid: People or pets with severe kidney disease, low potassium or gout.

name: Hydrocortisone
uses: Mild steroid for itchy, inflamed skin and in barrier ointments.
how: A mild steroid that reduces skin inflammation and itch.
avoid: Skin infections that are not being treated. Avoid long use on the face or thin skin.

name: Hydroquinone
uses: Dark spots and melasma.
how: Blocks tyrosinase, the enzyme that makes skin pigment.
avoid: Long-term continuous use, which can darken skin. Use sunscreen.
Pregnancy. Long-term continuous use, which can darken or thin the skin. Use sunscreen daily.
how: Hydroquinone blocks tyrosinase, the enzyme that makes skin pigment. Tretinoin speeds skin cell turnover and helps hydroquinone work, hydrocortisone calms irritation, and niacinamide reduces the transfer of pigment to the skin surface.
name: Hydroquinone 12% melasma cream
side: Irritation, redness, peeling and sun sensitivity. For limited-duration use with close prescriber follow-up.
uses: Stubborn melasma and dark spots. A high-strength cream made with hydroquinone 12%, tretinoin 0.05%, niacinamide 2% and hydrocortisone 2.5%.

avoid: Long-term continuous use, which can darken skin. Pregnancy. Use sunscreen daily.
how: Hydroquinone blocks tyrosinase, the enzyme that makes skin pigment. Vitamin C also slows pigment production, and niacinamide reduces the transfer of pigment to the skin surface.
name: Hydroquinone 5% melasma cream
side: Irritation or redness. For limited-duration use.
uses: Melasma and dark spots. Made with hydroquinone 5%, niacinamide 3% and vitamin C 1%.

name: Hydroxyzine
uses: Itch and anxiety.
how: An antihistamine that also has calming effects.
avoid: People with heart rhythm problems, and during early pregnancy.

name: Hyoscyamine
uses: Stomach and bowel cramping.
how: Blocks acetylcholine to relax smooth muscle in the gut and bladder.
avoid: People with glaucoma, bowel blockage or urinary retention.

name: Ibuprofen
uses: Pain and inflammation.
how: An NSAID that blocks COX enzymes to reduce inflammation and pain.
avoid: People with ulcers, kidney disease or late pregnancy. Toxic to dogs and cats.

name: Imatinib
uses: Certain cancers, including mast cell tumors in pets.
side: Vomiting, diarrhea, decreased appetite; hazardous drug.
how: Blocks specific tyrosine kinase enzymes that drive some cancers.
avoid: Pregnancy and liver disease. Hazardous drug: handle with gloves.

name: Imipenem
uses: Resistant bacterial ear infections in pets.
how: A carbapenem antibiotic that breaks down bacterial cell walls, reserved for resistant infections.
avoid: Pets with a beta-lactam allergy.

name: Itraconazole
uses: Fungal infections including ringworm.
how: Blocks the fungal enzyme needed to build the fungal cell membrane.
avoid: People or pets with liver disease or heart failure.

name: Ivermectin
uses: Parasites in animals; rosacea creams in people.
side: Neurologic effects in sensitive dog breeds; local irritation topically.
how: Paralyzes parasites by acting on their nerve and muscle channels; topically it calms rosacea.
avoid: Collies, Australian shepherds and other herding breeds with the MDR1 gene (oral use), and young animals.

name: Ketoconazole
uses: Fungal and yeast infections of skin, scalp and ears.
side: Local irritation; liver effects with oral use.
how: Blocks the fungal enzyme needed to build the fungal cell membrane; orally it also lowers cortisol.
avoid: People or pets with liver disease (oral use), and anyone taking cisapride.

name: Ketoprofen
uses: Anti-inflammatory used in topical pain creams.
how: An NSAID that blocks COX enzymes to reduce inflammation and pain.
avoid: People with NSAID allergies or ulcers. Keep topical forms away from pets.

name: Ketotifen
uses: Mast cell stabilizer for allergies and mast cell activation.
how: Stabilizes mast cells so they release less histamine and also blocks histamine receptors.
avoid: People with seizure disorders or diabetes (some forms).

name: Kojic acid
uses: Brightening creams for dark spots.
how: Blocks tyrosinase, the enzyme that makes skin pigment.
avoid: People with sensitive skin.

name: L-Arginine
uses: Amino acid used in topical circulation and sexual-health creams.
how: An amino acid the body uses to make nitric oxide, which relaxes blood vessels.
avoid: People with low blood pressure or a history of cold sores that flare easily.

name: L-Methionine
uses: Urinary acidifier for pets.
how: An amino acid that makes the urine more acidic.
avoid: Cats and dogs with liver or kidney disease, and young kittens.

name: Lansoprazole
uses: Reduces stomach acid.
how: A proton pump inhibitor that shuts down the stomach's acid pumps.
avoid: Long-term use can affect vitamin B12 and magnesium.

name: Leucovorin
uses: Folate supplement that protects against some medication side effects.
how: A ready-to-use form of folate.
avoid: People with untreated B12 deficiency.

name: Levetiracetam
uses: Seizure control in people, dogs and cats.
how: Binds a protein on nerve endings (SV2A) that controls the release of signals, calming abnormal electrical activity.
avoid: People with kidney disease or a history of depression or mood changes.

name: Levocetirizine
uses: Allergy relief.
how: An antihistamine that blocks H1 receptors.
avoid: People with kidney disease.

name: Levothyroxine (T4)
uses: Thyroid hormone replacement for hypothyroidism in people and dogs.
side: Signs of too much thyroid hormone: fast heartbeat, restlessness, weight loss.
how: A synthetic form of T4, the main hormone the thyroid gland makes.
avoid: People or pets with untreated adrenal insufficiency or heart disease (start low).

name: Lidocaine
uses: Numbing for skin, mouth and procedures; in pain creams and mouthwashes.
side: Temporary numbness, local irritation. Use only as directed on large areas.
how: Blocks sodium channels in nerves to stop pain signals temporarily.
avoid: Applying to large areas, broken skin or under wraps unless directed. Too much can affect the heart and nervous system.

name: Linezolid
uses: Resistant bacterial infections.
how: Blocks bacterial protein production; reserved for resistant infections.
avoid: Anyone taking MAO inhibitors or serotonin medicines.

name: Liothyronine (T3)
uses: Thyroid hormone replacement, sometimes combined with T4 in custom capsules.
how: A synthetic form of T3, the active thyroid hormone.
avoid: People with heart disease or untreated adrenal insufficiency.

name: Loratadine
uses: Allergy relief.
how: A non-drowsy antihistamine that blocks H1 receptors.
avoid: People with liver disease (lower dose). Some commercial forms contain decongestants unsafe for pets.

name: Lovastatin
uses: Topical cream with cholesterol for porokeratosis and other rare skin conditions.
how: Blocks cholesterol production in the skin, used with topical cholesterol for rare genetic skin conditions.
avoid: Pregnancy.

name: Magic mouthwash
uses: Blends of an antihistamine, antacid, numbing agent and sometimes antifungal or steroid for mouth sores, including from chemotherapy.
side: Temporary numbness, altered taste. Do not eat or drink right after use.
how: Combines a numbing agent, an antacid coating and an antihistamine, sometimes with an antifungal or steroid, to soothe mouth sores.
avoid: Swallowing the rinse when directed to spit, and eating or drinking before the numbness wears off.

name: Magnesium
uses: Magnesium supplement.
how: A mineral needed for muscle, nerve and heart function.
avoid: People or pets with kidney disease.

name: Marbofloxacin
uses: Bacterial infections in pets.
how: A fluoroquinolone that blocks bacterial DNA copying.
avoid: Young growing dogs and pets with seizures.

name: Maropitant
uses: Vomiting and motion sickness in dogs and cats.
how: Blocks substance P at the vomiting center in the brain.
avoid: Very young puppies and pets with liver disease.

name: Mastic gum
uses: Traditional supplement for stomach support.
how: A plant resin traditionally used to soothe the stomach.
avoid: People allergic to pistachio or mastic trees.

name: Mebendazole
uses: Intestinal worms.
how: Blocks worms from absorbing sugar, which kills them.
avoid: Pregnancy and liver disease.

name: Meclizine
uses: Motion sickness and vertigo.
how: An antihistamine that calms the inner ear and vomiting center.
avoid: People with glaucoma or urinary retention.

name: Melatonin
uses: Sleep support in people; hair loss and anxiety support in dogs.
how: Mimics the hormone the body makes to signal nighttime and regulate sleep cycles.
avoid: People with autoimmune conditions or seizure disorders. Some commercial products contain xylitol, which is toxic to dogs.

name: Meloxicam
uses: Arthritis and pain.
how: An NSAID that blocks COX-2 more than COX-1 to reduce inflammation.
avoid: People or pets with kidney disease, ulcers or dehydration, or taking steroids.

name: Metformin
uses: Type 2 diabetes and insulin resistance.
how: Lowers the liver's sugar production and helps the body respond to insulin.
avoid: People with kidney disease, severe liver disease or heavy alcohol use, and before contrast X-ray studies.

name: Methenamine hippurate
uses: Helps prevent recurring urinary tract infections.
how: Turns into formaldehyde in acidic urine, which prevents bacteria from growing.
avoid: People or pets with kidney or liver disease, or taking sulfa drugs.

name: Methimazole
uses: Hyperthyroidism in cats, including transdermal gel applied to the ear.
side: Vomiting, decreased appetite, facial itching; requires blood monitoring.
how: Blocks the thyroid gland from making thyroid hormone.
avoid: Cats with kidney disease need close monitoring, since treating hyperthyroidism can reveal kidney problems.

name: Methocarbamol
uses: Muscle spasm.
how: A muscle relaxant that acts on the central nervous system.
avoid: People or pets with kidney disease (injectable forms).

name: Metoclopramide
uses: Nausea and slow stomach emptying.
how: Blocks dopamine to reduce nausea and speeds stomach emptying.
avoid: People or pets with a bowel blockage, seizures or pheochromocytoma.

name: Metronidazole
uses: Anaerobic and parasitic infections and diarrhea; also in topical creams.
side: Nausea, metallic taste, decreased appetite; bitter taste in pets.
how: Damages DNA in anaerobic bacteria and some parasites.
avoid: Pregnancy (early), liver disease, and alcohol use. High doses can cause neurologic signs in pets.

name: Mexiletine
uses: Heart rhythm disorders in people and dogs.
how: Blocks sodium channels in the heart to steady abnormal rhythms.
avoid: People or pets with certain heart blocks or liver disease.

name: Milk thistle
uses: Liver support supplement.
how: Contains silymarin, an antioxidant thought to protect liver cells.
avoid: People with ragweed allergies.

name: Minocycline
uses: Bacterial infections, acne and rosacea.
how: A tetracycline antibiotic that stops bacteria from making proteins.
avoid: Children under 8 and pregnancy.

name: Minoxidil
uses: Hair regrowth, as topical solutions or low-dose oral capsules.
side: Scalp irritation, unwanted hair growth; oral forms can cause fluid retention or fast heartbeat.
how: Widens blood vessels and extends the hair's growth phase, which can thicken thinning hair.
avoid: People with heart disease or low blood pressure (oral forms). Very toxic to cats; keep topical forms away from pets.

name: Mirtazapine
uses: Depression and sleep in people; appetite stimulation and nausea control in cats and dogs, including transdermal gels.
side: Drowsiness, increased appetite, vocalization in cats.
how: Increases serotonin and norepinephrine signaling and blocks histamine, which boosts appetite and reduces nausea.
avoid: Pets or people with liver or kidney disease (lower doses needed), and anyone on MAO inhibitors.

name: Montelukast
uses: Asthma and allergies.
how: Blocks leukotrienes, inflammatory signals that tighten airways.
avoid: People with a history of depression or mood changes.

name: Mupirocin
uses: Topical and nasal preparations for bacterial skin infections, including MRSA.
how: Blocks an enzyme bacteria need to make proteins.
avoid: Usually well tolerated; for skin and nasal use only.

name: Mycophenolate
uses: Immune-mediated diseases.
how: Blocks the growth of immune cells.
avoid: Pregnancy, and people or pets with serious infections.

name: N-acetylcysteine (NAC)
uses: Antioxidant support; mucus thinning.
how: Replenishes glutathione, the body's main antioxidant, and breaks up thick mucus.
avoid: People with asthma (inhaled forms) or bleeding disorders.

name: Naltrexone (including low-dose)
uses: Low-dose naltrexone (LDN) is prescribed off-label for chronic pain, inflammation and autoimmune conditions; standard doses treat alcohol and opioid dependence.
side: Vivid dreams, trouble sleeping, headache, nausea. Blocks opioid pain relievers.
how: At standard doses it blocks opioid receptors. At low doses it briefly blocks them, which is thought to prompt the body to make more of its own endorphins and to calm certain immune cells.
avoid: Anyone taking opioid pain medicine or who needs opioids for surgery, and people with liver disease.

name: Neomycin
uses: Topical and ear preparations for bacterial infections.
how: An aminoglycoside that stops bacteria from making proteins.
avoid: Ruptured eardrums (ear products); some people develop skin allergies to it.

name: Niacinamide
uses: Skin tone, barrier and redness support in creams; vitamin B3.
how: A form of vitamin B3 that strengthens the skin barrier and evens tone.
avoid: Usually well tolerated.

name: Nifedipine
uses: Topical ointments for anal fissures and hemorrhoid pain.
how: Relaxes smooth muscle, easing the spasm that keeps anal fissures from healing.
avoid: People with very low blood pressure.

name: Nipple cream (APNO)
uses: A combination of an antibiotic, steroid and antifungal for sore, cracked nipples while breastfeeding, applied after feeding as directed.
how: Combines an antibiotic, a steroid and an antifungal to treat infection and inflammation of the nipple.
avoid: Wipe off before feeding only if your provider directs; use for the shortest time needed.

name: Nitrofurantoin
uses: Urinary tract infections.
how: Damages bacterial DNA and proteins, concentrated in the urine.
avoid: People or pets with kidney disease, and people near the end of pregnancy.

name: Nitroglycerin
uses: Topical ointment for anal fissures.
how: Releases nitric oxide, relaxing the anal sphincter muscle and improving blood flow to help fissures heal.
avoid: Anyone taking sildenafil, tadalafil or similar medicines. Headaches are common.

name: Nystatin
uses: Yeast infections of the mouth and skin, including mouthwash and ointments.
how: Binds to the yeast cell wall and makes it leak, killing the yeast.
avoid: Usually well tolerated; not absorbed into the body when swallowed.

name: Omeprazole
uses: Reduces stomach acid for reflux and ulcers.
how: A proton pump inhibitor that shuts down the stomach's acid pumps.
avoid: Long-term use can affect vitamin B12 and magnesium; interacts with clopidogrel.

name: Ondansetron
uses: Nausea and vomiting.
how: Blocks serotonin (5-HT3) receptors that trigger nausea.
avoid: People or pets with heart rhythm problems, and anyone taking apomorphine.

name: Oxymetazoline
uses: Facial redness from rosacea.
how: Narrows blood vessels in the skin to reduce redness.
avoid: Use as directed; overuse can cause rebound redness.

name: Oxytocin
uses: A naturally occurring hormone prescribed off-label as rapid-dissolve tablets, most often for sexual health and bonding.
how: Mimics the hormone oxytocin, which is involved in bonding, social behavior and sexual response.
avoid: Pregnancy.

name: Pantoprazole
uses: Reduces stomach acid, including suspensions for feeding tubes.
how: A proton pump inhibitor that shuts down the stomach's acid pumps.
avoid: Long-term use can affect vitamin B12 and magnesium.

name: Paroxetine
uses: Anxiety and depression; behavior problems in pets.
how: An SSRI that increases serotonin available in the brain.
avoid: Anyone taking MAO inhibitors or other serotonin medicines, and those who are pregnant.

name: Pentoxifylline
uses: Circulation support; used in topical sexual-health creams and in dogs for some skin and vascular conditions.
how: Makes red blood cells more flexible and blood less sticky, which improves circulation in small vessels.
avoid: People with recent bleeding or stroke, and those sensitive to caffeine or theophylline.

name: Phenobarbital
uses: Long-standing seizure medication for dogs and cats.
side: Sedation, increased thirst, appetite and urination; requires liver monitoring.
how: Boosts the brain's main calming signal (GABA), reducing seizure activity.
avoid: Pets with liver disease. Needs regular blood level and liver monitoring.

name: Phenoxybenzamine
uses: Urethral spasm and urine retention in cats and dogs.
how: Blocks alpha receptors to relax the urethra and blood vessels.
avoid: Pets with low blood pressure or heart disease.

name: Phenylephrine
uses: Constricts blood vessels; used in numbing ointments and hemorrhoid care.
how: Narrows blood vessels, which reduces swelling and bleeding.
avoid: People with high blood pressure or heart disease (larger amounts).

name: Phenylpropanolamine
uses: Urinary incontinence in dogs.
side: Restlessness, high blood pressure, decreased appetite.
how: Tightens the muscle that keeps the bladder closed.
avoid: Dogs with high blood pressure, heart disease or glaucoma.

name: Pilocarpine
uses: Dry mouth (lollipops and troches) and dry eye.
how: Stimulates saliva and tear glands.
avoid: People with asthma, glaucoma of certain types, or heart disease.

name: Pimobendan
uses: Congestive heart failure and certain heart diseases in dogs, and sometimes cats.
how: Strengthens the heart's squeeze and widens blood vessels, reducing the heart's workload.
avoid: Dogs with certain heart conditions where increasing the heart's force is harmful, such as some obstructive diseases.

name: Piroxicam
uses: Some bladder cancers and pain in dogs.
how: An NSAID that reduces inflammation and has anti-tumor effects in some cancers.
avoid: Pets with ulcers or kidney disease, or taking steroids.

name: Polymyxin B
uses: Topical and ear preparations for bacterial infections.
how: Disrupts the outer membrane of bacteria.
avoid: Ruptured eardrums (ear products).

name: Ponazuril
uses: Coccidia and protozoal infections in pets.
how: Blocks the energy production of protozoa such as coccidia.
avoid: Usually well tolerated.

name: Potassium bromide
uses: Seizure control in dogs.
side: Sedation, increased thirst and appetite, wobbliness.
how: Bromide replaces chloride in nerve cells, making them less excitable.
avoid: Cats (it can cause serious lung problems), and dogs with kidney disease or on low-salt diets.

name: Potassium chloride
uses: Potassium supplementation.
how: Replaces potassium.
avoid: People or pets with high potassium or kidney failure.

name: Potassium citrate
uses: Helps prevent certain kidney and bladder stones.
how: Makes urine less acidic and adds citrate, which blocks certain stones from forming.
avoid: People or pets with high potassium, kidney failure or stomach ulcers.

name: Potassium gluconate
uses: Potassium supplement for cats and dogs with low potassium, often from kidney disease.
how: Replaces potassium lost through the kidneys.
avoid: Pets with high potassium or urinary blockage.

name: Praziquantel
uses: Tapeworms and flukes in pets.
how: Makes tapeworm and fluke membranes leak calcium, paralyzing them.
avoid: Very young puppies and kittens.

name: Prazosin
uses: Urinary blockage and urethral spasm in cats and dogs; blood pressure and nightmares in people.
how: Blocks alpha-1 receptors, relaxing smooth muscle in blood vessels and the urethra.
avoid: People or pets with low blood pressure.

name: Prednisolone
uses: Inflammation, allergies and immune conditions; preferred over prednisone in cats.
side: Increased thirst, urination and appetite, panting, mood changes.
how: A steroid that calms inflammation and the immune system.
avoid: People or pets with diabetes, infections or stomach ulcers, or taking NSAIDs. Do not stop suddenly after long use.

name: Prednisone
uses: Inflammation, allergies and immune conditions.
side: Increased thirst, urination and appetite, mood changes.
how: A steroid the liver converts to prednisolone to calm inflammation and the immune system.
avoid: Cats and people with liver disease (prednisolone is preferred), and anyone with diabetes, infections or ulcers.

name: Pregabalin
uses: Nerve pain and fibromyalgia; seizures in pets.
how: Binds calcium channels on nerve cells and reduces the release of pain and excitement signals.
avoid: People with kidney disease, heart failure or a history of misuse.

name: Pregnenolone
uses: A hormone precursor occasionally included in hormone therapy plans.
how: A building block the body uses to make other steroid hormones.
avoid: People with hormone-sensitive cancers and those who are pregnant or breastfeeding.

name: Prilocaine
uses: Numbing agent in topical anesthetic creams.
how: Blocks nerve signals to numb the skin.
avoid: Infants and people with methemoglobinemia.

name: Progesterone
uses: Hormone therapy in women, often alongside estrogen, and for cycle and sleep support as prescribed.
side: Drowsiness, dizziness, breast tenderness, bloating, headache.
how: Replaces the hormone progesterone, which balances the effects of estrogen on the uterus and supports sleep and mood in some women.
avoid: People with a history of breast cancer, blood clots, stroke, liver disease or unexplained vaginal bleeding. Can cause drowsiness; oral forms are usually taken at bedtime.

name: Pyridostigmine
uses: Myasthenia gravis (muscle weakness) in people and dogs.
how: Slows the breakdown of acetylcholine, the chemical that tells muscles to contract.
avoid: People with bowel or urinary blockages or asthma.

name: Quetiapine
uses: Mood disorders and sleep, as prescribed.
how: Blocks dopamine and serotonin receptors and has sedating antihistamine effects.
avoid: Older adults with dementia, and people with heart rhythm problems or diabetes.

name: Rivaroxaban
uses: Prevents and treats blood clots.
how: Blocks factor Xa, a key step in blood clotting.
avoid: People or pets with active bleeding or severe liver disease.

name: Rosemary oil
uses: Ingredient in topical hair-growth serums.
how: A plant oil used in hair serums.
avoid: People with sensitive skin. Some essential oils are toxic to cats.

name: Rutin
uses: Supplement used in cats and dogs with chylothorax (fluid around the lungs).
how: A plant flavonoid thought to help the body clear fluid from the chest in chylothorax.
avoid: Usually well tolerated.

name: Sacubitril/valsartan
uses: Heart failure.
side: Low blood pressure, dizziness, high potassium.
how: Combines a blocker of angiotensin receptors with a drug that preserves natural hormones that relax vessels and remove fluid.
avoid: Pregnancy, and anyone taking an ACE inhibitor or with a history of angioedema.

name: Salicylic acid
uses: Warts, calluses and thick skin.
how: A beta hydroxy acid that softens and removes thick skin.
avoid: Large areas of skin, children, and people allergic to aspirin. Toxic to cats.

name: SAM-e
uses: Liver and joint support supplement.
how: A natural compound that supports liver cell repair and joint health.
avoid: People with bipolar disorder or taking antidepressants.

name: Scream Cream
uses: A topical cream for women, applied before intimacy, that combines theophylline, ergoloid mesylates, pentoxifylline and sildenafil (sometimes with L-arginine) to increase blood flow and sensitivity.
side: Warmth, tingling or redness where applied, and occasional headache.
how: Each ingredient increases local blood flow in a different way, which may improve arousal and sensitivity.
avoid: Anyone taking nitrates for chest pain, and people with low blood pressure or an allergy to any ingredient. Not for use during pregnancy.

name: Selegiline
uses: Cognitive dysfunction in older dogs and pituitary-dependent Cushing's.
how: Blocks MAO-B, an enzyme that breaks down dopamine in the brain.
avoid: Pets taking other behavior medicines such as fluoxetine or amitriptyline, or certain flea and tick products (amitraz).

name: Sertraline
uses: Anxiety and depression; behavior problems in pets.
how: An SSRI that increases serotonin available in the brain.
avoid: Anyone taking MAO inhibitors or other serotonin medicines.

name: Sildenafil
uses: Erectile dysfunction and topical sexual-health creams in people; pulmonary hypertension in dogs and cats.
side: Headache, flushing, nasal congestion, low blood pressure. Do not combine with nitrates.
how: Blocks PDE5, an enzyme that narrows blood vessels, which improves blood flow in the penis and lungs.
avoid: Anyone taking nitrates for chest pain or certain blood pressure medicines, and people with severe heart disease or very low blood pressure.

name: Sirolimus
uses: Immune suppression and some specialty uses.
how: Blocks mTOR, a signal that drives immune cell and tissue growth.
avoid: People with serious infections or poor wound healing.

name: Sodium butyrate
uses: Suppositories used for bowel inflammation such as proctitis.
how: A short-chain fatty acid that is the main fuel for cells lining the colon.
avoid: People with rectal bleeding that has not been evaluated.

name: Sotalol
uses: Heart rhythm disorders in people and dogs.
how: A beta-blocker with extra effects on the heart's electrical rhythm.
avoid: People or pets with asthma, slow heart rate or kidney disease; requires careful monitoring.

name: Spironolactone
uses: Heart failure and fluid buildup; hormonal acne and hair loss in women.
side: High potassium, breast tenderness, irregular periods.
how: Blocks the hormone aldosterone, helping the body shed fluid while holding onto potassium; also blocks some androgen effects.
avoid: People or pets with high potassium or kidney disease, and those who are pregnant.

name: Sucralfate
uses: Coats and protects ulcers and irritated tissue; used in mouthwash blends.
how: Forms a protective coating over ulcers and irritated tissue.
avoid: Give 2 hours apart from other medicines, since it can block their absorption.

name: Sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim
uses: Urinary, skin and other infections.
side: Stomach upset, dry eye in dogs, allergic reaction.
how: Two drugs that block bacteria from making folic acid.
avoid: Anyone with a sulfa allergy, liver disease or dry eye (dogs), and Doberman pinschers.

name: T4/T3 thyroid capsules
uses: Levothyroxine (T4) and liothyronine (T3) combined in one capsule, in the strengths and ratio your prescriber orders, including slow-release capsules.
side: Signs of too much thyroid hormone: fast heartbeat, anxiety, trouble sleeping, sweating or weight loss.
how: T4 is the storage form of thyroid hormone that the body converts into active T3. A combination capsule replaces both hormones together.
avoid: People with heart disease or untreated adrenal insufficiency. Your prescriber adjusts the dose based on your lab results.

name: Tacrolimus
uses: Immune-related skin and eye conditions.
how: Blocks activation of T cells in the skin or eye.
avoid: People or pets with active skin infections.

name: Tadalafil
uses: Erectile dysfunction, enlarged prostate symptoms and pulmonary hypertension.
side: Headache, flushing, back pain, low blood pressure. Do not combine with nitrates.
how: Blocks PDE5, relaxing smooth muscle and improving blood flow; it lasts longer than sildenafil.
avoid: Anyone taking nitrates for chest pain, and people with severe heart disease or very low blood pressure.

name: Tamsulosin
uses: Urinary flow problems from an enlarged prostate or urethral spasm.
how: Relaxes muscle in the prostate and bladder neck to improve urine flow.
avoid: People or pets with low blood pressure; people with a sulfa allergy should check with their prescriber.

name: Telmisartan
uses: High blood pressure in people and cats and kidney protein loss.
side: Dizziness, low blood pressure, changes in kidney values.
how: Blocks angiotensin receptors, relaxing blood vessels and protecting the kidneys.
avoid: Pregnancy, and people or pets with dehydration or high potassium.

name: Terbinafine
uses: Fungal skin and nail infections, including ringworm.
how: Blocks squalene epoxidase, an enzyme fungi need to build their membranes.
avoid: People or pets with liver or kidney disease.

name: Terbutaline
uses: Opens airways in asthma and feline asthma.
how: Relaxes airway muscles by stimulating beta-2 receptors.
avoid: People or pets with heart rhythm problems, high blood pressure or overactive thyroid.

name: Terconazole
uses: Vaginal yeast infections.
how: Blocks fungal cell membrane production.
avoid: Usually well tolerated; for vaginal use only.

name: Testosterone
uses: Hormone replacement for men and women with low testosterone, as prescribed and monitored by a clinician.
side: Skin irritation where applied, acne, oily skin, hair growth, mood changes; can transfer to others through skin contact.
how: Replaces or supplements the body's own testosterone, the main male sex hormone that is also present at lower levels in women.
avoid: People with prostate or breast cancer, those who are pregnant or trying to conceive, and people with high red blood cell counts. Keep treated skin away from children, partners and pets.

name: Tetracaine
uses: Numbing agent in topical anesthetic creams for procedures.
how: Blocks nerve signals to numb the skin.
avoid: Large areas or broken skin; allergy to ester-type numbing agents.

name: Tetracycline
uses: Bacterial infections, including vet ear preparations.
how: An antibiotic that stops bacteria from making proteins.
avoid: Children under 8 and pregnancy.

name: Theophylline
uses: Bronchodilator for asthma and airway disease; also an ingredient in topical sexual-health creams.
how: Relaxes airway muscles and increases blood flow; topically it is used for its circulation effects.
avoid: People with heart rhythm problems, seizures or stomach ulcers (oral use). Oral forms interact with many medicines.

name: Thiamine (vitamin B1)
uses: Vitamin B1 supplement.
how: Vitamin B1, needed for nerve and energy metabolism.
avoid: Usually well tolerated.

name: Thyroid (desiccated)
uses: Natural thyroid hormone replacement.
how: Dried thyroid gland that contains both T4 and T3 hormones.
avoid: People with heart disease or untreated adrenal insufficiency.

name: Tinidazole
uses: Parasitic and anaerobic infections.
how: Damages DNA in anaerobic bacteria and some parasites.
avoid: Pregnancy (early) and alcohol use.

name: Topiramate
uses: Seizures and migraine prevention.
side: Tingling, drowsiness, word-finding difficulty, taste changes.
how: Calms nerve activity through several pathways, including sodium channels and GABA.
avoid: People with kidney stones, glaucoma, or who are pregnant.

name: Torsemide
uses: Fluid buildup from heart failure.
how: A long-acting loop diuretic that makes the kidneys remove more salt and water.
avoid: People or pets who are dehydrated or have low potassium; needs kidney monitoring.

name: Tranexamic acid
uses: Brightening creams for dark spots and melasma; bleeding control.
how: Blocks plasmin, an enzyme involved in bleeding and in pigment production.
avoid: People with a history of blood clots (oral forms).

name: Trazodone
uses: Sleep and anxiety in people; calming before vet visits, travel and recovery in dogs and cats.
side: Drowsiness, low blood pressure, stomach upset.
how: Blocks certain serotonin receptors and has a calming, sleep-promoting effect.
avoid: People or pets taking other serotonin medicines, and those with heart rhythm problems.

name: Tretinoin
uses: Acne, sun damage, fine lines and dark spots.
side: Dryness, peeling, sun sensitivity. Avoid in pregnancy.
how: A vitamin A derivative that speeds skin cell turnover and unclogs pores.
avoid: Pregnancy. Increases sun sensitivity.
Pregnancy. Long-term continuous hydroquinone use, which can darken skin. Use sunscreen daily.
how: Tretinoin speeds skin cell turnover, hydroquinone blocks tyrosinase (the enzyme that makes skin pigment), niacinamide reduces pigment transfer and supports the skin barrier, and hyaluronic acid holds moisture.
name: Tretinoin and hydroquinone chest cream
side: Dryness, peeling, irritation and sun sensitivity.
uses: Sun damage, dark spots and fine lines on the chest. Made with tretinoin 0.01%, hydroquinone 7%, niacinamide 3% and hyaluronic acid 0.5%.

avoid: Pregnancy. Use sunscreen daily.
how: Tretinoin speeds skin cell turnover and supports collagen, niacinamide supports the skin barrier and evens tone, and hyaluronic acid holds moisture.
name: Tretinoin neck cream
side: Dryness, peeling, redness or sun sensitivity.
uses: Fine lines, crepey texture and uneven tone on the neck. Made with tretinoin 0.03%, niacinamide 3% and hyaluronic acid 0.5%.

avoid: Pregnancy. Getting it in the eyes. Use sunscreen daily.
how: Tretinoin speeds skin cell turnover, caffeine tightens small blood vessels to reduce darkness and puffiness, hyaluronic acid holds moisture, and niacinamide supports the skin barrier and evens tone.
name: Tretinoin under-eye serum
side: Dryness, mild peeling, redness or sun sensitivity.
uses: Dark circles and fine wrinkles under the eyes. A gentle serum made with tretinoin 0.001%, caffeine 1%, hyaluronic acid 2% and niacinamide 2%.

name: Triamcinolone
uses: Steroid for skin and ear inflammation, including vet ear packs.
how: A medium-strength steroid that reduces inflammation.
avoid: Untreated skin or ear infections; avoid long use on thin skin.

name: Trichloroacetic acid (TCA)
uses: A strong acid applied by a clinician in the office for chemical peels and to treat warts and some skin lesions.
side: Burning, redness and peeling; for professional application only.
how: Causes controlled peeling of the outer skin layers.
avoid: Home use. For application by a trained clinician only.

name: Trilostane
uses: Cushing's disease (hyperadrenocorticism) in dogs.
side: Lethargy, decreased appetite, vomiting; requires monitoring.
how: Blocks an enzyme in the adrenal gland to lower cortisol production.
avoid: Dogs with kidney or liver disease, and pregnant dogs.

name: Tylosin
uses: Chronic diarrhea and colitis in dogs.
how: A macrolide antibiotic that also changes gut bacteria in dogs with chronic diarrhea.
avoid: Horses and rabbits. Extremely bitter, so it is usually compounded into capsules.

name: Urea
uses: Thick, dry or cracked skin and nails; ear flush ingredients.
how: Draws water into skin and softens thick, rough areas.
avoid: Broken or irritated skin.

name: Ursodiol
uses: Liver and gallbladder conditions and gallstones.
how: A natural bile acid that makes bile thinner and protects liver cells.
avoid: People or pets with a blocked bile duct.

name: Valacyclovir
uses: Herpes infections, cold sores and shingles.
how: Converted to acyclovir, which stops herpesviruses from copying their DNA.
avoid: People with kidney disease (lower dose).

name: Vitamin C
uses: Antioxidant in skin creams; vitamin supplement.
how: An antioxidant that brightens skin and supports collagen.
avoid: Usually well tolerated.

name: Vitamin E
uses: Antioxidant supplement and skin moisturizer.
how: An antioxidant that protects cell membranes.
avoid: People taking blood thinners (high oral doses).

name: Zonisamide
uses: Seizure control, often as an add-on medication.
how: Blocks sodium and calcium channels in nerve cells to reduce abnormal electrical activity.
avoid: Anyone allergic to sulfa drugs, and people with kidney stones or kidney disease.
